S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.

subtypes.Feeling Keyed Up: Feeling anxious and wound up like a spring, unable to stay still.
subtypes.Physical Tension: The entire body feels stiff and tense, unable to relax.
subtypes.Nervousness: Nerves are on edge, being startled easily by minor sounds or stimuli.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.

subtypes.Neck and Shoulder Tension: Muscles in the shoulders and back of the neck are knotted and stiff, causing pain or headaches.
subtypes.Jaw Tension: Clenching teeth or tension in the jaw causing jaw pain or headaches.
subtypes.Generalized Muscle Aches: Muscles all over the body, including back, arms, and legs, are stiff, painful, and easily fatigued.
subtypes.Chronic Stiffness: Muscles remain in a constant state of tension and do not relax.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent and excessive worry about multiple domains of life (e.g., work, health, finances, family) occurring more days than not for at least six months, and is difficult for the individual to control. The anxiety is accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations such as feeling keyed up, fatigue, impaired concentration, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance, leading to clinically significant distress or functional impairment. The course is often chronic and fluctuating, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stressors but a baseline tendency toward pervasive apprehension. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by its broad, free-floating worry (rather than discrete panic attacks, specific phobias, or circumscribed obsessions) and by the absence of prominent compulsive rituals or trauma-focused re-experiencing.

patient.personality: Dario is a methodical, intellectually curious technologist who prides himself on craftsmanship and mentoring while juggling a wide range of creative hobbies.
patient.stressor: About eight months ago, Dario was promoted into a lead role on a high-visibility cloud migration project with an aggressive timeline, just as his company began quietly hinting at future restructuring. Accustomed to controlling details in his code and personal projects, he found himself responsible for coordinating multiple teams, managing ambiguous requirements, and fielding late-night messages from stakeholders in different time zones, all while trying to remain the calm expert his junior colleagues expected. Over the next several months, he increasingly brought work home—mentally rehearsing failure scenarios, replaying small mistakes, and adding more side projects in an effort to stay "ahead," which began to crowd out the restorative routines that had previously helped him decompress. When he noticed that his constant mental preoccupation with potential problems was eroding his concentration, slowing his coding, and making him irritable and unavailable with his spouse, he agreed at her urging to seek psychiatric help.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel constantly keyed up, like I can’t ever switch my brain or body off.”

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I sleep a full night and don’t stay late at the office, I feel like I’m wading through wet concrete, and just getting through a normal workday leaves me so drained that I end up collapsing on the couch instead of working on my usual side projects or even talking much with my wife.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: My brain is constantly running simulations about work and money and the company restructuring—like I’ll be in the shower and suddenly I’m picturing how a small deployment bug could snowball into us missing the deadline, the project getting blamed on me, and then somehow we lose the house because I can’t find another job in this market.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: I keep telling myself to just shut it off and focus on whatever’s in front of me, but the ‘what ifs’ barge back in within minutes, and before I know it I’ve gone from thinking about one risky API change to spiraling through a whole chain of disasters I know are irrational but can’t stop replaying.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.
S058.manifestation: Most of the time I feel like I’ve had three espressos too many—my leg’s bouncing under the desk, I’m checking Slack and email obsessively, and even when I sit down to play guitar or watch a show, there’s this wired, on‑edge feeling like I’m waiting for something to go wrong.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.
S061.manifestation: By the end of most days my shoulders and neck are so tight from hunching over my laptop and clenching without realizing it that I get these dull tension headaches, and my wife will have to remind me to actually stretch because my body feels like it’s been bracing for impact all day.
